name: UAE Federal Decree-Law 10/2025 + Cabinet Resolution 134/2025 (AML/CTF/PF)
supervisor: CBUAE + EOCN-AML/CTF + SCA + MOE + DFSA + FSRA + VARA (per scope)

chapters.title: Customer Due Diligence + Enhanced Due Diligence + PEPs

articles.title: Designated persons + sectoral scope
articles.requirement: Captures: Financial Institutions (banks, finance companies, insurers, payment service providers, money exchange houses, hawala providers — supervised by CBUAE; securities + commodities firms supervised by SCA; DIFC FIs supervised by DFSA; ADGM FIs supervised by FSRA); VASPs (per CBUAE / SCA / DFSA / FSRA / VARA scope); DNFBPs (real-estate agents, dealers in precious metals + stones, lawyers + notaries + accountants, corporate service providers, etc. — supervised by MOE primarily). Multi-regulator architecture; same federal substantive obligations apply across regulators.

articles.title: Multi-regulator architecture
articles.requirement: Firms operating across multiple UAE jurisdictions face simultaneous regimes: federal CBUAE / SCA / MOE (onshore UAE); DIFC DFSA (DIFC); ADGM FSRA (ADGM); Dubai VARA (Dubai excluding DIFC, VA-only). Each regulator issues its own sectoral AML guidance + supervisory expectations; the federal FDL 10/2025 substantive obligations operate as the baseline. Cross-regulator program design + coordination is a distinct compliance discipline.

articles.title: Customer Due Diligence (Art. 5-6)
articles.requirement: CDD applied: at establishment of a business relationship; on occasional transactions ≥ AED 55,000 (~US$15,000) — or AED 3,500 (~US$1,000) for wire transfers; on suspicion of ML/TF/PF; on doubts about prior CDD adequacy. Measures: identify + verify customer + UBO using reliable independent sources; understand purpose + intended nature; conduct ongoing monitoring (transaction scrutiny + record refresh). Risk-based intensity. Reliance on third-party CDD subject to conditions (regulated + supervised + immediate-information-access + ultimate-responsibility-retained).

articles.title: Enhanced Due Diligence (Art. 7)
articles.requirement: EDD required for: foreign + domestic + IO PEPs; high-risk jurisdictions (FATF-identified + UAE national identifications); complex / unusual / large transactions without apparent economic / legal purpose; correspondent banking with respondent banks in higher-risk jurisdictions; new products + business practices including new delivery mechanisms + new technologies (incl. crypto / DeFi exposure). Senior-management approval; SoW + SoF verification; enhanced ongoing monitoring; documented rationale. CR 134/2025 prescribes specific operational requirements per risk category.

articles.title: PEP obligations (Art. 8)
articles.requirement: Foreign PEPs: always heightened risk + full EDD. Domestic PEPs (federal-level officials, senior emirate-level officials, federal court judges, senior military / police, leadership of state-owned enterprises): risk-sensitive assessment — typically still triggering EDD for politically-significant positions. International organisation PEPs: similar risk-sensitive treatment. Family members + close associates within scope; 12-month tail after PEP function ends. EOCN-AML/CTF advisories provide operational guidance on PEP categorisation.

articles.title: Beneficial Ownership (Art. 10-11)
articles.requirement: Identify + verify the beneficial owner of every customer (legal entity, legal arrangement, trust). 25% ownership / voting / control threshold + senior-managing-official fallback. UAE BO registry maintained by Ministry of Economy + sector-specific registries; FIs may access for CDD purposes. Particular focus on complex group structures + nominee arrangements + foundations. Operational requirements per CR 134/2025 + supervisor guidance.

articles.title: Proliferation Financing controls (Art. 12)
articles.requirement: Expanded vs FDL 20/2018. PF risk assessment as a distinct dimension of the entity-wide RBA + customer risk profile (aligns with FATF R.1 + R.7 updates). Controls for UN-designated entities (DPRK + Iran focus); dual-use goods + sensitive-technology trade-finance scrutiny; sanctions-evasion typology training; integration with sanctions screening. EOCN-AML/CTF issues operational PF guidance.

articles.title: Suspicious Activity Reporting via goAML (Art. 15)
articles.requirement: Designated persons must report to the FIU UAE via the goAML platform without delay on knowledge or reasonable suspicion of ML / TF / PF or related predicate offences. Structured XML / form-based submission per CR 134/2025 + goAML guidance. Tipping-off prohibition (FDL 10/2025 Art 17). Statutory immunity for good-faith reports. Operational + format updates vs predecessor framework; emphasis on quality + timeliness.

articles.title: Tipping-off prohibition (Art. 17)
articles.requirement: Designated persons + staff prohibited from disclosing to a customer or third party that an SAR has been filed or that an ML/TF investigation may be carried out. Carve-outs: sharing with supervisors (CBUAE / DFSA / FSRA / VARA / SCA) + within group on need-to-know for ML/TF purposes + legal advice. Criminal sanction for breach.

articles.title: Sanctions + targeted financial measures (Art. 18-19)
articles.requirement: Mandatory screening against UN Security Council Consolidated List + the UAE Local Terrorist List + targeted UAE designations. Real-time customer + transaction screening; freeze + report regime; cooperation with EOCN-AML/CTF + Federal Public Prosecution. Continued operational focus following October 2024 FATF grey-list exit. Particular operational focus on DPRK + Iran + Russia / Belarus where international + UAE designations overlap.

articles.title: Internal organisation + AML compliance officer (Art. 20-21)
articles.requirement: Documented written policies + procedures + senior-management approval; designated AML compliance officer (MLRO) at sufficient seniority + independence + resources + access to senior management; internal audit + compliance-function review of the AML programme. Transaction-monitoring + screening systems calibrated to the risk assessment + tuned periodically. Supervisor (CBUAE / DFSA / FSRA / VARA / SCA / MOE) approves the AML compliance officer where required.

articles.title: Training (Art. 22)
articles.requirement: All employees with AML/CFT/PF-relevant responsibilities trained on: applicable laws + FDL 10/2025 + CR 134/2025 + internal policies; current ML/TF/PF typologies + red flags (incl. PF-specific scenarios); their role in the AML/CFT framework; how to escalate suspicion; tipping-off prohibition. Refresher training on regulatory + typology changes. Records retained; training-effectiveness assessment (testing or scenario-based).

articles.title: Record retention — 5 years minimum (Art. 23)
articles.requirement: CDD documentation + business correspondence + transaction records + SAR working papers retained for at least 5 years after the end of the business relationship or the completion of the occasional transaction; longer where ongoing investigation or supervisory request. Records sufficient to enable reconstruction of individual transactions + accessibility to FIU UAE + supervisors on request.

articles.title: Sanctions + supervisory measures (Art. 25-30)
articles.requirement: Administrative + criminal sanctions: administrative fines (substantially increased vs predecessor — supervisor-imposed CMPs up to AED 5m for the most serious failings); licence suspension or withdrawal; prohibition orders against individuals; remediation orders; criminal sanctions for ML offences (imprisonment + asset forfeiture) + tipping-off (imprisonment + fine). Multi-regulator enforcement coordination via EOCN-AML/CTF. Post-grey-list-exit enforcement intensity continues.

articles.title: Transition from FDL 20/2018 + CD 10/2019
articles.requirement: Existing CBUAE + DFSA + FSRA + VARA + SCA + MOE supervisor guidance issued under FDL 20/2018 continues to apply where not inconsistent with FDL 10/2025 + CR 134/2025. Legacy relationships established under FDL 20/2018 transitioned per CR 134/2025 — refresh of risk assessment + customer risk profile required, but not automatic re-onboarding. Supervisors expect documented transition plans + tracking through the post-14-October-2025 period.
